HANDBOOK.md: A Benchmark for Long-Context Agentic Instruction Following

paper.arxiv.2607.25398

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2607.25398v3. Two-sided deterministic criteria and fictional-company task construction establish evaluation/data workflow. Variant-specific handbooks and snapshot/configuration differences do not create extra families. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The study uses fictional company environments, expert-mutated policies, mock services and one common OpenHands harness under explicit call/time caps. Policy mutation is intended to resist memorization; the protocol does not by itself prove uncontaminated pretraining or establish naturalistic corporate compliance and safety outside these tasks.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2607.25398.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Experts adapt ten industry handbooks into 65 fictional-company tasks with per-task operative policy mutations. Handbooks span 20-124 rendered pages and arrive as PDF, Word or HTML.
  • Eight hundred twenty-four deterministic Python criteria check final workspace/service state, including required outputs and prohibited behavior. No LLM judging is used; strict pass requires all criteria, with four trials per task and a separate N-minus-one metric.
  • Task builders iterate tasks and criteria against repeated model runs. A common OpenHands harness caps each trial at 200 tool calls and one hour; provider/transport errors are excluded and rerun.
  • July Table 2 has thirty configurations, while the cost/efficiency section refers to twenty configurations evaluated at release. Strict and relaxed metrics remain separate.
  • Industry-policy inspiration and mock services do not constitute observation of actual private corporate work or an independent audit of pretraining contamination or deployment safety.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

HANDBOOK.md describes 65 tasks using mutated expert-written 20–124-page policies and 824 programmatic criteria over final workspace/service state. Required outputs and prohibited behavior are checked separately; strict pass@1 requires every criterion and averages four trials per task, while N−1 is a separately labeled relaxed metric.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The frozen July 2026 Table 2 reports a highest strict pass@1 of 36.2% among 30 evaluated model/configuration entries on 65 tasks with four trials each. This is the averaged all-criteria trial metric in one specified harness, not a fraction of unique tasks permanently unsolvable or a current vendor ranking.
